messages:
sanjay: Quick follow-up to the autoscale RFC: TL;DR and a few open decisions. Need to finalize today so eng-sre can start work.

claire: Can we split "prewarm" vs "reserved" capacity? Prewarm = ephemeral warm replicas; reserved = billed committed GPUs.

drew: Strong yes. Operationally they behave differently (eviction, billing, admission). Prewarm must be preemptible.

luis: I sketched a minimal policy DSL so product/ops can read configs. Example:
```
policy "embedding-video-low-latency" {
  min_reserved: 4
  prewarm: { target: 2, idle_ttl_sec: 300 }
  burst: { limit: 6, burst_window_sec: 120 }
  drain: { protect_sec: 120, force_after_sec: 600 }
  admission: "latency-first"
}
```

claire: How do we express tenant overrides? Some customers want dedicated prewarm but not billed as reserve.

luis: We'll support per-org overrides via API. Precedence: org_override > pool_policy > default.

maria: Ops: when we drain hosts for kernel updates, prewarmed slots get pulled immediately today which kills warmups. Can't do that. Suggest marking slots as "protected" during drain for small window so in-flight work finishes.

sanjay: Agree. Default protect_sec=120. Also need to ensure scheduler won't reassign those protected slots until expire.

drew: Autoscaler implications: protected slots should not count toward scaledown triggers; otherwise the scaler will thrash. We'll add metric: protected_drain_active.

luis: Prewarm sizing tradeoff: use a 7-day 95th percentile for baseline but include a stability factor (recent node churn, error rate). We should expose a knob: prewarm_aggressiveness.

claire: From billing: reserved vs prewarm labels must be unambiguous. Finance needs tags emitted with allocation events.

opsbot: Created ticket RN-4789 for drain protection work: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RN-4789

drew: Metrics to add: prewarm_hits, prewarm_misses, prewarm_evictions, burst_peak, protected_drain_failures. Alert on prewarm_evictions > 2x baseline.

sanjay: Owners: eng-runtime (API + policy parser) - @luis; eng-sre (autoscaler + drain semantics) - @drew; product/finance for billing labels - @claire; ops to schedule maintenance sync - @maria.

claire: Rollout plan: feature flag + canary on low-traffic pools, observe prewarm_hit rate and cost delta before wider rollout.

sanjay: I'll produce a short RFC appendix with DSL grammar, acceptance criteria, migration notes, and a rollout checklist. Ping me on the doc for final sign-off.

claire: Thanks, include an experiment to compare prewarm_aggressiveness at 95th vs 99th percentile.

sanjay: will do. :thumbsup:
